Roles
MediumRole guide

Top Lane

The island: long 1v1 duels, tough champions, and a lane that can carry the whole map.

You'll enjoy this role if…

  • You enjoy pure 1v1 battles where your skill decides the lane.
  • You like tough champions who can take a beating and keep swinging.
  • You don't mind being a bit alone, away from the rest of your team.
  • You like the idea of one player pulling three enemies to the side of the map.

What this role does

Top lane is the solo lane at the top of the map. Top laners are usually durable fighters or tanks who win long duels, pressure side lanes, and either lead the charge or protect the team in fights.

  • Win or hold your lane against one opponent, mostly without help.
  • Farm well: top laners need levels and items to fight.
  • Use Teleport or your role quest's free Teleport to join fights in other lanes.
  • Pressure the side lanes in the mid game so the enemy has to send people to stop you.
  • In teamfights, either start the fight (tanks) or dive the enemy backline (fighters).

Champion types

Most top laners fit into a few families. Knowing which one you're playing tells you how to win:

  • Juggernauts and bruisers like Garen, Darius and Sett deal big damage and are hard to kill. They want long fights up close.
  • Tanks like Malphite and Ornn soak damage and start fights with powerful crowd control. They scale into teamfight monsters.
  • Scaling champions like Nasus are weak early but become terrifying late if they farm safely.
  • Skirmishers and duelists like Fiora and Camille win 1v1 fights with clever mechanics. They're rewarding but harder to learn.
  • Ranged top laners like Teemo and Kennen annoy melee champions by hitting them from a distance.

If you're new, start with a bruiser or tank. They forgive mistakes, because you can survive a bad trade.

Early game (levels 1-6)

Top lane is long, so ganks take time to arrive and escapes are hard. That makes the early game a careful dance.

  • Start: most fighters start Doran's Blade or Doran's Shield plus a Health Potion. Take Doran's Shield if the matchup is hard.
  • Farm first. Every minion is gold and experience you need. Read Last-Hitting 101 if you miss a lot.
  • Trade when your opponent goes for a minion. Their attention is on the last hit, so that's your window. See Trading in Lane.
  • Watch the level 2 and level 3 races. The first wave gives you level 2 a little before the second wave finishes. Being level 2 first is a free chance to hit your opponent.
  • Respect the jungler. If you push far up the lane without vision, you're easy to gank. Ward the river brush or the tri-bush around 2:30-3:00, when the enemy jungler may arrive.

You don't have to win every lane. A good top laner knows when the matchup is bad and just farms safely under tower.

Pro tipFreezing the wave near your own tower is the top laner's best defensive tool. Your opponent has to walk far forward to farm, which makes them easy prey for your jungler. Learn it in Wave Management: Push, Freeze and Crash.

Your role quest

In 2026 every player automatically gets a quest for their assigned position. You fill it by farming, breaking plates, taking turrets and objectives, getting takedowns and simply spending time in your lane.

The top lane quest needs 1200 points. When it's done you get:

  • Unleashed Teleport as a bonus summoner spell (390s cooldown). If you already took Teleport, it instead gets a shield worth 35% of your max health and a shorter cooldown.
  • +600 bonus experience, +11% experience from everything, and +80 experience per takedown.
  • A level cap of 20 instead of 18, so you can out-level everyone late in the game.

Because the quest gives you a free Teleport, many top laners now take Ignite or Ghost alongside Flash to be stronger in lane.

Common mistakeLeaving lane early to roam is costly. Minion gold and experience outside your lane are reduced by 25% until level 3, and you lose quest progress while you're away. Stay in lane early unless there's a clear kill to get.

Mid game: side lanes and Teleport

Around 14 minutes, the outer turrets start falling and the game opens up. Top laners have two jobs now:

  • Split pushing: push the top side lane so the enemy has to send someone to stop you. If one player comes, you might win the 1v1. If two or three come, your team can take an objective somewhere else. See Side Lanes & Split Pushing.
  • Teleport plays: watch the map for fights near dragon or in bot lane. A well-timed Teleport onto a ward or minion behind the enemy can win the fight for your team.

The Rift Herald spawns at 15:00 in the top side pit and leaves at 19:45. Top laners are often closest to it, so help your jungler take it. Ride the Herald into a turret for huge damage.

Remember: turret plates no longer fall off in 2026, so pressuring turrets stays rewarding all game.

Late game and teamfights

Late in the game, a single fight can decide everything. Your job depends on your champion:

  • Tanks: start the fight. Look for an engage that catches several enemies, like Malphite's ultimate. Then stand between your carries and the enemy divers.
  • Fighters: wait for the enemy to use their crowd control, then dive their carries or fight whoever is closest. Going in first as a fighter usually means getting stunned and dying.
  • Split pushers: keep pressure on a side lane, but stay close enough to join your team when Baron or Elder Dragon is up. Teleport helps here.

If you're behind, become useful anyway: build tanky items and focus on protecting your carries or catching out a lone enemy.

Advanced tips

  • Track the enemy jungler's start. If they started bot side, you have a safe window to push early. See Tracking the Enemy Jungler.
  • Learn matchup power spikes. Know which levels or items make you stronger than your opponent, and fight then. Matchups, Cooldowns & Lane Priority covers how.
  • Bounce the wave. Crashing a big wave into the enemy tower before you recall means you don't lose minions while you shop.
  • Track the enemy Teleport. If theirs is on cooldown and yours isn't, your team has a numbers advantage in the next fight. Ping it.
  • Proxy farming (farming behind the enemy's turret) is an advanced trick for fast-clearing champions to draw enemies away from objectives.

Beginner-friendly champions

GarenSimple kit, heals himself, very forgiving. The classic first top laner.
MalphiteTanky rock with one of the easiest game-winning ultimates to use.
SettStrong, straightforward brawler who wins most early fights up close.
NasusTeaches you to farm: every last hit with Q makes him stronger forever.
OrnnTank who builds item upgrades for the whole team. Great for learning teamfights.

Common mistakes

  • Pushing up the lane with no wards and dying to a gank over and over.
  • Fighting your opponent when they're at a power spike (a new level or item) and you aren't.
  • Forgetting you have Teleport and staying in lane while your team fights 4v5.
  • Chasing a kill under the enemy tower at low health.
  • Ignoring the map in the mid game: split pushing while the enemy team takes Baron.
  • Roaming too early and losing farm, experience and quest progress.
